- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is below recent high, increase forecast by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1) and forecast is above recent low, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3 days.  
- If sentiment swings from negative to positive within 3 days, model often underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% on day of sentiment shift.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 2σ above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by > 3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias of 0.5–1% to next forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ negative values in row), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1% lag correction to forecast.
